source: NCERT Class XII, India — People and Economy, Ch. 4 (Human Settlements).

sections.heading: 1. Settlements — Rural and Urban
points: A **settlement** = a place where people live; classified as **rural** and **urban**.
**Rural settlements** — closely and directly related to **land/agriculture**; smaller, primary activities.
**Urban settlements** — larger, engaged in secondary/tertiary activities; higher density.

sections.heading: 2. Types of Rural Settlements
points: Patterns depend on relief, water, security, culture.

sections.heading: 3. Urban Settlements and Classification
points: In India, an **urban area** is defined by population (5000+), density (400/sq km) and % in non-agricultural work (75%+ male workers).
**Classification by function:** administrative, industrial, transport, commercial, mining, garrison, educational, religious, tourist towns.
**Class of towns by size** (Class I = 1 lakh+, up to Class VI); **metropolitan cities** (1 million+); **megacities** (10 million+ — Mumbai, Delhi, Kolkata).

sections.heading: 4. Urbanisation and Problems
points: **Urbanisation** — the growing share of population living in towns/cities.
Problems: **slums, housing shortage, congestion, pollution, water/sanitation, unemployment, crime**.
Smart cities, urban planning and infrastructure aim to address these.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Rural patterns: clustered, semi-clustered, hamleted, dispersed.
Indian urban area: 5000+ population, 400/sq km density, 75% non-agri male workers.
Class I town = 1 lakh+; metropolitan = 1 million+; megacity = 10 million+.
Urban problems: slums, congestion, pollution, sanitation.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Clustered (nucleated) settlements** occur in fertile plains; **dispersed** in hills/forests.
An Indian **Class I town has 1 lakh+ population**; a **metropolitan city has 1 million+**.
Urban areas are defined by population, density AND % non-agricultural workers.
